findings.what_the_code_does: In the working tree, `MATCHING/results/profile_names_jw.md` is modified and truncated at exactly 4,096 bytes, ending mid-heading at line 31 (`## Men, death month on profile: first name and s` with no trailing newline) and deleting four complete tables (47 lines) present in `HEAD`. In addition, `MATCHING/_run_profile_names_jw.do` and `MATCHING/_run_tgt_fallback_diag.do` (temporary wrappers generated by `replication/Run-Stata.ps1:30`) are present as untracked (`??`) files because `_run_*.do` is not matched by `.gitignore`.

findings.how_to_check: After loading a state in `MATCHING/nomodel_diag.do`, run `tab img_n if img_n<=5` and compare `count if ftype==t & img_fail>0.5` against the leave-one-out rate `count if ftype==t & (img_fail*img_n - fail)/(img_n - 1) > 0.5 & img_n > 1`, as well as against image failure computed before line 30's `keep if`.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute full-image size and failure rate before line 30's `keep if` (over all rows on `filename`), and for target-record image clustering compute the leave-one-out failure share among *other* records on the image (`(sum_fail - fail)/(img_n - 1)` for `img_n > 1`, reporting `img_n == 1` separately) so a record's own failure status does not mechanically drive `"Image mostly failing (%)"`.
findings.title: `img_fail` includes each record in its own image-level failure mean after dropping concordant records, creating a mechanical disparity in `"Image mostly failing (%)"` across columns
findings.what_the_code_does: Line 30 filters to discordant human-complete records (`keep if namefrst!="" & namelast!="" & fs_namefrst!="" & fs_namelast!="" & !(namefrst==fs_namefrst & namelast==fs_namelast)`), and lines 34-36 then compute `gen byte fail = ftype>0`, `bysort filename: egen double img_fail = mean(fail)`, and `bysort filename: gen long img_n = _N`. Lines 104-110 tabulate `"Image mostly failing (%)"` (`img_fail > 0.5`) across `ftype == 0` (`fail == 0`, "Both names") and `ftype == 1, 2, 3` (`fail == 1`, the three no-output categories).
findings.why_it_matters: Because `img_fail` is computed after dropping ~73% of lines (concordant records) and includes record $i$'s own `fail` indicator in `(fail_i + sum_{j!=i} fail_j)/img_n`, comparing `img_fail > 0.5` across groups defined by `fail_i == 0` (`ftype == 0`) vs. `fail_i == 1` (`ftype > 0`) has a severe mechanical bias whenever `img_n` is small. On any image with `img_n == 1` target record, `img_fail > 0.5` is identically 0% for `ftype == 0` and identically 100% for `ftype in {1,2,3}` even when zero other records on the image failed. On any image with `img_n == 2` target records, `img_fail` for `ftype == 0` is at most `1/2 = 0.5` (so `img_fail > 0.5` is still mechanically 0%), whereas for `ftype in {1,2,3}` it exceeds `0.5` whenever the single other target record fails. This overstates image-level clustering of model failures relative to `Both names`.

findings.how_to_check: Run `count if filename==""` and `bysort st filename linep: count if _N>1` across the appended dataset in `MATCHING/nomodel_diag.do`.
findings.suggested_fix: Check for empty `filename` (`count if filename==""`) inside the state loop and compute `bysort filename: egen double img_fail = mean(fail) if filename!=""` and `bysort filename: gen long img_n = _N if filename!=""`, reporting records with `filename==""` separately rather than pooling them into one image group.
findings.title: `bysort filename:` does not exclude empty `filename == ""`, which would pool all unmatched records in a state into one synthetic image
findings.what_the_code_does: Lines 35-36 run `bysort filename: egen double img_fail = mean(fail)` and `bysort filename: gen long img_n = _N` without asserting `filename != ""` or restricting to non-empty `filename`.
findings.why_it_matters: In Stata, `bysort filename:` groups all rows with `filename == ""` in a state into a single group. If any target records in `merged_data.dta` have `filename == ""` (e.g., human census records that did not link to an ML image record when `merged_data.dta` was built, all of which have `ftype == 1`, "Both empty"), every such record in the state gets assigned `img_fail = 1.0` (`> 0.5`) and `img_n` equal to the state's total unmatched target record count $M$. In the record-weighted mean at line 114 (`quietly sum img_n if ftype==1`), those $M$ records contribute $M^2$ to the sum, distorting both `"Mean target records per image"` and `"Image mostly failing (%)"`. Furthermore, `MATCHING/profile_names_build.log:733-740` shows `merged_data.dta` has 128,837 duplicate human-complete rows sharing a `histid`, which also inflate `img_n` on affected images.

findings.title: Unquoted `` `v'==`val' `` in `levelsof` loop will crash if `non_ditto_ml` is stored as a string variable
findings.what_the_code_does: Lines 120-139 iterate `foreach v in non_ditto non_ditto_ml`, extract distinct values via `quietly levelsof `v', missing local(vals)`, and count matches at line 134 with `quietly count if ftype==`t' & `v'==`val'`.
findings.why_it_matters: `non_ditto` is constructed as numeric (`1` or `.`) in `CODE/clean_FS_and_combineV5_nber.do:100`, whereas `non_ditto_ml` comes from the external ML pipeline (`merged_data.dta`). If `non_ditto_ml` is stored as a string variable, `foreach val of local vals` strips quotes from `levelsof` tokens: an empty-string level `""` expands line 134 to `quietly count if ftype==0 & non_ditto_ml==` (`r(198)` syntax error) and non-empty string levels expand to unquoted tokens (`r(109)` type mismatch or `r(111)` not found), aborting the script after all 49 states have been loaded and leaving `MATCHING/results/nomodel_diag.md` partially written.

structured_output.summary: The working tree contains a truncated tracked results file (`MATCHING/results/profile_names_jw.md`, cut off mid-heading at a 4,096-byte buffer boundary while a background Stata job is still running, alongside two untracked `_run_*.do` wrapper files) that would corrupt committed results if pushed via `Sync.ps1`. In the staged new diagnostic script `MATCHING/nomodel_diag.do`, the image-clustering measure (`img_fail > 0.5`) is computed after filtering to discordant target records and includes each record in its own image failure mean, creating a severe mechanical own-observation bias across columns on images with few target records (`img_n` of 1 or 2). `MATCHING/nomodel_diag.do` also lacks a guard against empty `filename == ""` in `bysort filename:` (which would pool all unmatched records in a state into a single huge synthetic image) and uses an unquoted `levelsof` comparison on `non_ditto_ml`.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
